--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+# backup_rotate.py
+
+`backup_rotate.py` is a tool for creating timestamped archives of a directory and managing their retention through rotation policies or age-based pruning.
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+python3 backup_rotate.py [GLOBAL_OPTIONS] COMMAND [COMMAND_OPTIONS]
+```
+
+### Global Options
+
+| Option | Description | Default |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `-v`, `--verbose` | Log each file considered to stderr | `False` |
+| `--version` | Print version and exit | - |
+
+### Commands
+
+#### `create`
+
+Archives a directory into the backup directory.
+
+**Arguments:**
+
+| Argument | Description |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `source` | The directory to archive |
+
+**Options:**
+
+| Option | Description | Default |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `-d`, `--backup-dir` | Directory that holds the archives (can be set via `BACKUP_ROTATE_DIR` environment variable) | `"backups"` |
+| `--prefix` | Archive name prefix; archives with other prefixes are never touched | `"backup"` |
+| `--format` | Archive format (`tar.gz` or `zip`) | `"tar.gz"` |
+| `--exclude` | Glob matched against relative paths and each path component (repeatable) | `[]` |
+
+**Example:**
+
+```bash
+python3 backup_rotate.py create my_source_dir --backup-dir my_backups --format zip
+```
+
+---
+
+#### `plan`
+
+Shows which archives the retention policy keeps.
+
+**Options:**
+
+| Option | Description | Default |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `-d`, `--backup-dir` | Directory that holds the archives (can be set via `BACKUP_ROTATE_DIR` environment variable) | `"backups"` |
+| `--prefix` | Archive name prefix; archives with other prefixes are never touched | `"backup"` |
+| `--keep-daily` | Keep the newest archive of each of the last N days | `7` |
+| `--keep-weekly` | Keep the newest archive of each of the last N ISO weeks | `4` |
+| `--keep-monthly` | Keep the newest archive of each of the last N calendar months | `12` |
+| `--json` | Print the plan as JSON | `False` |
+
+**Example:**
+
+```bash
+python3 backup_rotate.py plan --backup-dir my_backups --json
+```
+
+---
+
+#### `apply`
+
+Removes archives that the retention policy drops.
+
+**Options:**
+
+| Option | Description | Default |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `-d`, `--backup-dir` | Directory that holds the archives (can be set via `BACKUP_ROTATE_DIR` environment variable) | `"backups"` |
+| `--prefix` | Archive name prefix; archives with other prefixes are never touched | `"backup"` |
+| `--keep-daily` | Keep the newest archive of each of the last N days | `7` |
+| `--keep-weekly` | Keep the newest archive of each of the last N ISO weeks | `4` |
+| `--keep-monthly` | Keep the newest archive of each of the last N calendar months | `12` |
+| `-n`, `--dry-run` | Only print what would be removed | `False` |
+| `--trash` | Move archives into `DIR/.trash/` instead of deleting them | `False` |
+
+**Example:**
+
+```bash
+python3 backup_rotate.py apply --backup-dir my_backups --trash
+```
+
+---
+
+#### `prune`
+
+Removes archives older than a specified cutoff.
+
+**Options:**
+
+| Option | Description | Default |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `-d`, `--backup-dir` | Directory that holds the archives (can be set via `BACKUP_ROTATE_DIR` environment variable) | `"backups"` |
+| `--prefix` | Archive name prefix; archives with other prefixes are never touched | `"backup"` |
+| `--max-age` | Remove archives older than N days | `90` |
+| `--min-keep` | Never remove the newest N archives, however old | `3` |
+| `-n`, `--dry-run` | Only print what would be removed | `False` |
+
+**Example:**
+
+```bash
+python3 backup_rotate.py prune --backup-dir my_backups --max-age 30
+```

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+import re
+from collections import Counter
+
+log_file = 'logs/access.log'
+
+# Regex to parse the log line
+# Example: 203.0.113.140 - - [14/Oct/2026:00:23:12 +0000] "POST /login HTTP/1.1" 302 0 "-" "Mozilla/5.0" 0.244
+# Group 1: Date/Time, Group 2: Method, Group 3: Path, Group 4: Status
+log_pattern = re.compile(r'.*?\[(.*?)\] "(.*?) (.*?) .*?" (\d{3})')
+
+def parse_log():

tasks.finalAnswer:
The test `test_pick_sheet_single_zone` in `tests/test_picklist.py` is failing.

**Why it fails:**
The `group_by_zone` function in `warehouse/picklist.py` uses a mutable default argument `groups={}`. In Python, default arguments are evaluated only once at function definition time, meaning the same dictionary object is shared across all calls to `group_by_zone` that do not provide an explicit `groups` argument. This causes the `groups` dictionary to accumulate data from previous tests, leading to extra stops being returned in subsequent calls.

**Line responsible:**
The line responsible is in `warehouse/picklist.py`:
```python
def group_by_zone(lines, groups={}):
```
